messages.subject: Announcement: New CRAN release - v2.2.0
messages.body_plain:
camtrapR version 2.2.0 is now available on CRAN. It is the first update on CRAN in almost 2 years and contains all changes that accumulated on GitHub since then, e.g.:
community (multi-species) occupancy models (with a new vignette)
optical character recognition for reading data field in images
improved camera operation matrices
many bugfixes and other small improvements
For a full list of changes, see:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/news/news.html

Installation as usual via:
install.packages("camtrapR")

If there are any issues with the new release, please let me know.

messages.subject_clean: Subsetting time series for camopPlot function
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I have a question concerning the subsetting of my camera operation data.
I have a camera trap setup running through several seasons (e.g. from 2017 until 2020), but I would like to have only a specific period for a seperate analyses (e.g. only 2019).
How can I "subset" the data for a camopPlot that shows only 2019?
What seemed to me quite easy turned out to be quite a task to me. Can anybody help?
Thanks,
Martin

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Subsetting time series for camopPlot function
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Subsetting time series for camopPlot function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Martin,

assuming you have a camera trap table (from which you create the camera operation matrix), just subset the camera trap table to the season of interest, create the camera operation matrix for that season and use camopPlot.

For example,

data(camtrapsMultiSeason)
camtrapsMultiSeason_2009 <- camtrapsMultiSeason[camtrapsMultiSeason$session == 2009,]
camop_2009 <- cameraOperation(camtrapsMultiSeason_2009, setupCol = "Setup_date", retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date", dateFormat = "dmy")
camtrapR:::camopPlot(camop_2009)

There are of course other ways also, e.g. using the index of the desired season in the respective column in the camera table to subset an existing camera operation matrix that contains all seasons.

Or use the internal function camtrapR:::deparseCamOpRownames() to parse the row names of the full camera operation matrix for subsetting, e.g.

camop <- cameraOperation(camtrapsMultiSeason, setupCol = "Setup_date", retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date", dateFormat = "dmy", sessionCol = "session")

camtrapR:::deparseCamOpRownames(camop)

Best,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] DateTime error
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

fixDateTimeOriginal() is for situations where the date/time tag was written to the MakerNotes instead of the Exif part of image metadata, and simply copies it over. That happens in a few Reconyx models.

To be sure I'd suggest to check the image metadata and try to find the DateTimeOriginal field. Either use exifTagNames(), or check with a recent version of digiKam which includes ExifTool (right side of the screen "Metadata" tag, then "ExifTool" tag).

In normal images you should see "DateTimeOriginal" in the "Exif" group. If it is absent under "Exif", but present under "MakerNotes", you can fit it with fixDateTimeOriginal(). If it is generally absent (e.g. images downloaded from image sharing websites have their metadata scrubbed), things will get more complicated.

So please let us know if you can find DateTimeOriginal anywhere for those images.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Issue creating camera operation with mutliple problem periods
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lydia,

I was not able to reproduce your problem, and cameraOperation() worked with the code you sent in v.2.2.0.

Do you have package lubridate installed and loaded? Maybe also try updating lubridate. as.duration() is a lubridate function, so the problem comes from that direction.

Below is the output from the code you shared, plotted with camtrapR:::camopPlot(). Left side is your code, right side is with camerasIndependent= T (for test purposes).

Blue is high effort, turqoise intermediate, and yellow 0. Does this look correct?

Also, the file name in your code is different from the file name you shared. So please make sure that the data frames match.

And also, I see your table uses column names "start" and "end" for your setup and retrieval column. These are also used by an intermediate step inside the function that calculates the duration of problem periods. Try renaming your setup/retrieval columns and see if the error persists.

Best regards,

Jürgen
